objectives.en: Contrast cytokinesis in animal and plant cells.

narration.en: Tender coconut water is liquid endosperm in which the nucleus divided again and again but the cytoplasm never did. What happens when cytokinesis is skipped?
narration.kn: ಎಳನೀರು ದ್ರವ ಭ್ರೂಣಪೋಷಕ; ಅದರಲ್ಲಿ ಕೋಶಕೇಂದ್ರ ಪದೇ ಪದೇ ವಿಭಜನೆಯಾದರೂ ಜೀವದ್ರವ್ಯ ವಿಭಜನೆಯಾಗಲಿಲ್ಲ. ಜೀವದ್ರವ್ಯ ವಿಭಜನೆ ನಡೆಯದಿದ್ದರೆ ಏನಾಗುತ್ತದೆ?

body.en: Mitosis divides the duplicated chromosomes into daughter nuclei; the cell itself is divided by cytokinesis. In an animal cell a furrow appears in the plasma membrane and deepens until it joins in the centre, dividing the cytoplasm in two. Plant cells have a rigid wall, so wall formation starts in the centre of the cell and grows outward to meet the existing lateral walls. It begins with a simple precursor, the cell plate, which becomes the middle lamella between the walls of adjacent cells. Organelles such as mitochondria and plastids are distributed between the daughters. When karyokinesis is not followed by cytokinesis, a multinucleate condition called a syncytium results, e.g. the liquid endosperm of coconut.

points.en: Animal cell: furrow from outside inward.
Plant cell: cell plate from the centre outward.
Syncytium: many nuclei, one cytoplasm (coconut endosperm).

narration.kn: ಪ್ರಾಣಿ ಜೀವಕೋಶದಲ್ಲಿ ಪ್ಲಾಸ್ಮಾ ಪೊರೆಯಲ್ಲಿ ತೋಡು ಉಂಟಾಗಿ ಜೀವದ್ರವ್ಯ ವಿಭಜನೆಯಾಗುತ್ತದೆ. ಸಸ್ಯ ಜೀವಕೋಶದಲ್ಲಿ ಕೋಶಫಲಕ ಮಧ್ಯದಿಂದ ಹೊರಗಡೆಗೆ ಬೆಳೆಯುತ್ತದೆ. ಜೀವದ್ರವ್ಯ ವಿಭಜನೆ ಆಗದಿದ್ದರೆ ಬಹುಕೋಶಕೇಂದ್ರೀಯ ಸಿನ್‌ಸೀಷಿಯಂ ಉಂಟಾಗುತ್ತದೆ.

title.en: Two ways to split the cytoplasm

narration.en: Let us compare cytokinesis in an animal cell and a plant cell.

say.en: In an animal cell a furrow appears in the plasma membrane and deepens from the outside inwards until the cell is pinched in two.
A plant cell has a rigid wall, so a cell plate forms in the centre and grows outwards to meet the side walls.
If karyokinesis is not followed by cytokinesis, one cell gets many nuclei: a syncytium, like the liquid endosperm of coconut.
Mitosis is an equational division: both daughter cells get the same chromosomes as the parent. That is why it matters so much.

body.en: Mitosis usually occurs in diploid cells, though in some lower plants and social insects haploid cells also divide by mitosis. It produces diploid daughter cells with identical genetic complement. Growth of multicellular organisms depends on it. It restores the nucleo-cytoplasmic ratio, which is disturbed as a cell grows. It repairs and replaces cells: the upper layer of the epidermis, the lining of the gut and blood cells are constantly replaced. Mitosis in the apical and lateral cambium meristems gives continuous growth of plants throughout their life.

points.en: Growth, repair and replacement of cells.

problem.en: A single cell divides by mitosis repeatedly, and every daughter divides each round. How many mitotic divisions are needed to get 128 cells, and how many rounds of division does that take?

steps.en: Each round doubles the number of cells: after n rounds there are 2ⁿ cells.
Total number of individual divisions = 128 − 1 = 127 (each division adds one cell).

answer.en: 7 rounds of division; 127 individual mitotic divisions
